r2_py_py001.title: PY001 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py001.statement: Find the second largest distinct number in the list. Duplicate values should not affect the result.
r2_py_py001.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.

starter.python:
numbers = [10, 40, 20, 40, 30]
numbers.sort()
print("Second Largest:", numbers[-2])
starter.cpp:
numbers = [10, 40, 20, 40, 30]
numbers.sort()
print("Second Largest:", numbers[-2])

r2_py_py001.corrected_code:
numbers = [10, 40, 20, 40, 30]
unique_numbers = sorted(set(numbers))
print("Second Largest:", unique_numbers[-2])
r2_py_py001.answer_explanation: The list contains duplicate values. The program must remove duplicates before finding the second largest number.

r2_py_py002.title: PY002 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py002.statement: Remove all even numbers from the list while keeping the remaining numbers in their original order.
r2_py_py002.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.
r2_py_py002.corrected_code:
numbers = [2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9]
numbers = [n for n in numbers if n % 2 != 0]
print(numbers)
r2_py_py002.answer_explanation: Removing elements from a list while iterating over the same list can skip elements. A list comprehension creates the required filtered list safely.

r2_py_py003.title: PY003 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py003.statement: Correct the program to count the number of vowels in the given string.
r2_py_py003.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.

starter.python:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count =+ 1

print("Vowels:", count)
starter.cpp:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count =+ 1

print("Vowels:", count)

r2_py_py003.corrected_code:
text = "programming"
vowels = "aeiou"
count = 0

for char in text:
    if char in vowels:
        count += 1

print("Vowels:", count)
r2_py_py003.answer_explanation: The operator =+ assigns positive 1 instead of incrementing the existing value. The correct increment operator is +=.

r2_py_py004.title: PY004 – Debugging Challenge
r2_py_py004.statement: Correct the program to calculate the factorial of a number using a loop.
r2_py_py004.input_format: No additional input is required unless shown in the starter code.

starter.python:
number = 5
factorial = 0

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)
starter.cpp:
number = 5
factorial = 0

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)

r2_py_py004.corrected_code:
number = 5
factorial = 1

for i in range(1, number + 1):
    factorial *= i

print("Factorial:", factorial)
r2_py_py004.answer_explanation: Factorial multiplication must start with 1. Starting with 0 makes every multiplication result 0.

r3_py_py002.title: Largest of Three Numbers
r3_py_py002.statement: Write a program to find the largest among three integers.
r3_py_py002.input_format: Use the input format demonstrated by the test cases.

starter.python:
a, b, c = map(int, input().split())

largest = a

if b < largest:
    largest = b

if c < largest:
    largest = c

print(largest)
starter.cpp:
a, b, c = map(int, input().split())

largest = a

if b < largest:
    largest = b

if c < largest:
    largest = c

print(largest)

r3_py_py002.corrected_code:
a, b, c = map(int, input().split())

largest = a

if b > largest:
    largest = b

if c > largest:
    largest = c

print(largest)
r3_py_py002.answer_explanation: The program incorrectly checks whether b and c are smaller than the current largest value. To find the largest value, each number must be compared using >.

r3_py_py003.title: Sum of Digits
r3_py_py003.statement: Write a program to find the sum of the digits of a given positive integer.
r3_py_py003.input_format: Use the input format demonstrated by the test cases.

starter.python:
number = int(input())
sum_digits = 0

while number > 0:
    digit = number % 10
    sum_digits = digit
    number = number // 10

print(sum_digits)
starter.cpp:
number = int(input())
sum_digits = 0

while number > 0:
    digit = number % 10
    sum_digits = digit
    number = number // 10

print(sum_digits)

r3_py_py003.corrected_code:
number = int(input())
sum_digits = 0

while number > 0:
    digit = number % 10
    sum_digits += digit
    number = number // 10

print(sum_digits)
r3_py_py003.answer_explanation: The program replaces sum_digits with every digit instead of adding each digit to the existing sum. The += operator is required.

r3_py_py004.title: Second Largest Distinct Number
r3_py_py004.statement: Given an array of N integers, find the second largest distinct number. If a second largest distinct number does not exist, print -1.
r3_py_py004.input_format: Use the input format demonstrated by the test cases.

starter.python:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

numbers.sort(reverse=True)

if n < 2:
    print(-1)
else:
    print(numbers[1])
starter.cpp:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

numbers.sort(reverse=True)

if n < 2:
    print(-1)
else:
    print(numbers[1])

r3_py_py004.corrected_code:
n = int(input())
numbers = list(map(int, input().split()))

unique_numbers = sorted(set(numbers), reverse=True)

if len(unique_numbers) < 2:
    print(-1)
else:
    print(unique_numbers[1])
r3_py_py004.answer_explanation: The second largest value must be distinct. Sorting the original array and selecting index 1 fails when the largest value occurs more than once. Duplicate values must be removed before selecting the second largest value.
